qa.e: Both are true; managing through its own board under the Companies Act gives more flexibility.

qa.q: Which form would be MOST suitable for an enterprise that needs flexibility, wants to bring in private shareholders and should be quick to set up?
qa.a: Government company
qa.e: A company form is easy to set up and allows up to 49% private holding.

qa.q: Setting up public sector units in backward areas served the role of
qa.a: regional balance
qa.e: Locating industries in backward areas aimed at balanced regional development.

qa.q: Disinvestment means
qa.a: selling part of the government's equity in public enterprises to private investors and the public
qa.e: It is the reverse of investment: the government reduces its shareholding.

qa.q: A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the government and a public enterprise aims to
qa.a: give more autonomy to management while holding it accountable for results
qa.e: MoUs set targets and grant autonomy, linking freedom with accountability.

qa.q: Producing goods within the country that were earlier imported was the public sector's role of
qa.a: import substitution
qa.e: Import substitution aimed at self-reliance.

qa.q: Under the 1991 policy, sick public sector units were referred to
qa.a: the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR)
qa.e: Under the 1991 policy, BIFR examined whether sick units should be revived or closed. (BIFR was abolished in 2016; the National Company Law Tribunal now handles such cases.)

qa.q: Why did the public sector take up industries like steel and heavy machinery after Independence?
qa.a: They needed huge investment and gave economies of scale that private firms then could not provide
qa.e: Large capital needs and long gestation made public investment necessary.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The government reduced the number of industries reserved for the public sector after 1991. Reason (R): The 1991 policy aimed to open industries to private enterprise to increase efficiency and competition.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; the aim of greater competition explains why reservations were cut.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Disinvestment increases the government's shareholding in public enterprises. Reason (R): Disinvestment was one of the measures of the 1991 industrial policy.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: disinvestment reduces government shareholding. R is true.

qa.q: A global enterprise is
qa.a: a huge organisation operating in several countries under a global strategy, controlled from its headquarters
qa.e: MNCs operate across many countries through branches and subsidiaries.

qa.q: 'Centralised control' as a feature of MNCs means
qa.a: the head office in the home country controls all branches and subsidiaries
qa.e: Policies are framed at headquarters within an overall strategy.

qa.q: Which feature helps MNCs develop new products ahead of competitors?
qa.a: Product innovation through research and development
qa.e: MNCs invest heavily in R&D.

qa.q: MNCs enter into agreements with host-country firms for sharing technology, brands and patents. This feature is
qa.a: foreign collaboration
qa.e: Foreign collaboration means technical and other agreements with local firms.

qa.q: Which is NOT a feature of global enterprises?
qa.a: Operations limited to one city
qa.e: MNCs by definition operate across borders.

qa.q: Why can MNCs raise funds easily?
qa.a: Because of their huge size, reputation and access to many sources such as equity, debt and banks worldwide
qa.e: Their financial strength and creditworthiness allow easy fund-raising.

qa.q: Assertion (A): MNCs are able to maintain global quality standards. Reason (R): MNCs use advanced technology in their production.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; advanced technology is what enables global quality standards.

qa.q: Assertion (A): MNCs operate in a single country. Reason (R): MNCs follow aggressive marketing strategies.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: MNCs operate across many countries. R is true.

qa.q: A joint venture is formed when
qa.a: two or more independent firms pool resources for a common purpose
qa.e: JVs combine resources and share ownership, control and risk.

qa.q: A foreign firm forms a JV with an Indian firm mainly to use the Indian firm's dealer network. This benefit is
qa.a: access to new markets and distribution networks
qa.e: The Indian partner's network opens the market to the foreign firm.

qa.q: Public-private partnership (PPP) involves
qa.a: allocation of tasks, obligations and risks between public and private partners
qa.e: PPP shares responsibilities between the two sectors.

qa.q: In a PPP highway project, which is typically the government's contribution?
qa.a: Land, approvals and policy support
qa.e: The government provides land and regulatory support; the private partner builds and operates.

qa.q: Which sector is a typical area for PPP projects?
qa.a: Roads and ports
qa.e: Large infrastructure is the main field for PPP.

qa.q: Using a partner's cheaper local labour and raw materials gives a JV the benefit of
qa.a: low cost of production
qa.e: Local inputs reduce production costs.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Joint ventures help firms innovate. Reason (R): Partners bring different ideas, skills and technology together.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; combining different expertise is what sparks innovation.

qa.q: Assertion (A): In PPP, the private partner is responsible for the social obligations of the project. Reason (R): PPP allocates tasks and risks between public and private partners.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the government generally handles social obligations; the private partner focuses on efficiency. R is true.

qa.q: A customer customises his pizza toppings while ordering. Which feature of services does this show?
qa.a: Involvement
qa.e: The customer participates in shaping the service.

qa.q: A doctor's consultation is produced and consumed at the same time. This feature is
qa.a: inseparability
qa.e: Production and consumption of services happen together.

qa.q: Two customers get different experiences from the same salon on the same day. Which feature explains this?
qa.a: Inconsistency
qa.e: Service quality varies with time, provider and customer.

qa.q: Which of the following is a difference between goods and services?
qa.a: Goods can be stored, but services cannot
qa.e: Services are perishable; goods can be kept in inventory.

qa.q: Banking, insurance and warehousing are examples of
qa.a: business services
qa.e: Firms use them to carry out business activities.

qa.q: An NGO runs free eye-check camps in villages. This is a
qa.a: social service
qa.e: Social services are provided voluntarily to achieve social goals.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Services cannot be stored. Reason (R): Services are intangible and production and consumption occur together.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; because services are performed and consumed at once, there is nothing to store.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Ownership is transferred when a customer pays for a service. Reason (R): Services are experiential in nature.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: a service gives an experience, not ownership. R is true.

qa.q: Under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, a bank is an institution that
qa.a: accepts deposits from the public for lending or investment, withdrawable by cheque, draft or order
qa.e: Accepting deposits and lending them is the core of banking.

qa.q: Which is the central bank of India?
qa.a: Reserve Bank of India
qa.e: The RBI is India's central bank and regulator of the banking system.

qa.q: A bank pays 5% on deposits and charges 9% on loans. On ₹20,00,000 deposited and fully lent, what is its interest margin?
Bank drafts and pay orders are used for
qa.a: remittance of funds
qa.e: They transfer money safely from one place or person to another.

qa.q: Which of these is an allied service offered by commercial banks?
qa.a: Safe deposit lockers
qa.e: Lockers, bill payments and share dealings are allied services.

qa.q: A bank in which the government holds the majority of shares is a
qa.a: public sector bank
qa.e: Majority government ownership makes it a public sector bank.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Commercial banks are an important source of short-term finance for business. Reason (R): Commercial banks lend through overdrafts, cash credit and short-term loans.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; these lending forms are why banks are key short-term financiers.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The Reserve Bank of India accepts savings deposits from the general public. Reason (R): The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of the country.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the RBI is the bankers' bank and the government's bank, not a bank for the general public. R is true.

qa.q: Which account is most suitable for a businessman with a large number of daily transactions?
qa.a: Current account
qa.e: Current accounts have no limit on transactions and may offer overdraft.

qa.q: A salaried employee wants to deposit a fixed sum every month for five years. She should open a
qa.a: recurring deposit account
qa.e: An RD takes fixed monthly instalments for a fixed period.

qa.q: In a multiple option deposit account,
qa.a: surplus above a set limit in savings is automatically moved into a fixed deposit
qa.e: It combines savings-account liquidity with FD interest.

qa.q: Ajay's current account balance is ₹15,000 and his overdraft limit is ₹50,000. He withdraws ₹45,000. On what amount will he pay overdraft interest?
qa.e: He overdraws 45,000 − 15,000 = ₹30,000; interest is charged only on this.

qa.q: A trader has a cash credit limit of ₹5,00,000 against stock but uses only ₹2,00,000 during the period. Interest is charged on
qa.e: In cash credit, interest is charged on the amount actually used.

qa.q: A pay order (banker's cheque) is generally used for
qa.a: payment within the same city
qa.e: Pay orders are used locally; drafts are typically used for outstation payments.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A fixed deposit earns a higher rate of interest than a savings account. Reason (R): In a fixed deposit, money is kept with the bank for a fixed period, so the bank can lend it for longer.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; because the bank can use the funds for a fixed longer period, it pays more interest.

qa.q: Which lending facility is linked to a current account and lets the holder withdraw more than his balance up to a limit?
qa.a: Overdraft
qa.e: Overdraft allows overdrawing a current account up to a sanctioned limit.

qa.q: Which e-banking service settles each transaction individually and in real time?
qa.a: RTGS
qa.e: RTGS = Real Time Gross Settlement.

qa.q: In NEFT, funds are settled
qa.a: in batches
qa.e: NEFT works on deferred settlement in batches.

qa.q: When you pay with a debit card, the amount is
qa.a: deducted immediately from your bank account
qa.e: A debit card draws directly on the account balance.

qa.q: Which is a benefit of e-banking to banks?
qa.a: Less load on branches due to centralised databases
qa.e: Banks benefit by handling more transactions with fewer branch visits.

qa.q: E-banking creates a sense of financial discipline because
qa.a: every transaction is recorded and can be tracked
qa.e: A complete record of transactions helps customers track spending.

qa.q: A credit card allows the cardholder to
qa.a: buy now on credit up to a limit and pay the bank later
qa.e: Credit cards provide short-term credit up to a sanctioned limit.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-banking provides an unlimited network to banks. Reason (R): Customers can access banking services from anywhere through the internet, without visiting a branch.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; internet access removes the limit set by the number of branches.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-banking services are available only during branch working hours. Reason (R): E-banking uses the internet and electronic networks.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: e-banking is available 24 × 7. R is true.

qa.q: Which digital payment mode works on basic mobile phones without internet?
qa.a: USSD
qa.e: USSD banking uses the code *99#.

qa.q: UPI was developed by
qa.a: the National Payments Corporation of India
qa.e: NPCI runs UPI and other retail payment systems.

qa.q: Which payment mode uses Aadhaar authentication at micro ATMs?
qa.a: AEPS
qa.e: AEPS = Aadhaar Enabled Payment System.

qa.q: A card-swiping machine at a supermarket checkout is a
qa.a: Point of Sale (PoS) terminal
qa.e: PoS terminals accept card payments at shops.

qa.q: Business correspondents use small handheld devices to give basic banking in remote villages. These are
qa.a: micro ATMs
qa.e: Micro ATMs extend banking to areas without branches.

qa.q: A key feature of UPI is that it
qa.a: links multiple bank accounts into a single mobile app for instant transfers
qa.e: UPI allows instant transfers using a virtual payment address.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Digital payments reduce the need to carry cash. Reason (R): Payments are made electronically from bank accounts, cards or wallets.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; electronic transfer replaces physical cash.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A bank prepaid card allows spending beyond the amount loaded on it. Reason (R): A bank prepaid card is loaded with money in advance.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: you can spend only the loaded amount. R is true.

qa.q: In an insurance contract, the premium is paid by
qa.a: the insured to the insurer
qa.e: The insured pays the premium as consideration for cover.

qa.q: Insurance is based on the principle of
qa.a: pooling of risk
qa.e: Many contribute to a fund that compensates the few who suffer loss.

qa.q: 5,000 farmers pay ₹800 each into a crop insurance pool. What is the size of the pool?
Which function of insurance is shown when premiums are invested in long-term projects?
qa.a: Assisting in capital formation
qa.e: Accumulated premiums are invested, helping capital formation.

qa.q: Insurance gives 'protection' in the sense that it
qa.a: protects against the financial loss from an event, not against the event itself
qa.e: It compensates loss; it cannot prevent the risk.

qa.q: The document containing the terms of an insurance contract is called the
qa.a: policy
qa.e: The policy contains the terms and conditions of the contract.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Insurance helps share risk. Reason (R): The loss suffered by a few is spread over all those who pay premiums into the pool.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; spreading the loss over many is what risk sharing means.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Insurance prevents the loss from happening. Reason (R): Insurance compensates the insured for loss covered by the policy.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: it does not prevent loss. R is true.

qa.q: Ravi hides the fact that his godown stores highly inflammable chemicals while taking a fire policy. Which principle is violated?
qa.a: Utmost good faith
qa.e: Material facts must be disclosed honestly.

qa.q: The principle of indemnity does NOT apply to
qa.a: life insurance
qa.e: Loss of life cannot be measured in money, so life insurance is not a contract of indemnity.

qa.q: A property worth ₹10,00,000 is insured with X for ₹6,00,000 and with Y for ₹4,00,000. A loss of ₹5,00,000 occurs. How much will X pay?
qa.e: Under contribution, X : Y = 6 : 4 = 3 : 2. X pays 3/5 of ₹5,00,000 = ₹3,00,000.

qa.q: After paying a claim for a stolen car, the insurer gets the right to recover the car if it is later found. This is the principle of
qa.a: subrogation
qa.e: The insurer steps into the shoes of the insured after paying.

qa.q: A storm breaks a ship's mast; days later, sea water enters through the damage and spoils the cargo. The policy covers storm damage. Under proximate cause, the cargo loss is decided by
qa.a: the nearest direct cause of the loss and whether that cause is covered
qa.e: Causa proxima looks at the direct, effective cause of the loss.

qa.q: Goods worth ₹4,00,000 are insured for ₹4,00,000. Fire destroys goods worth ₹1,50,000. Under indemnity, the insured gets
qa.e: Only the actual loss is compensated.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A person can take a life policy on the life of his spouse. Reason (R): A person has an insurable interest in the life of his spouse.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; the insurable interest in the spouse's life is why such a policy is allowed.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Under the principle of indemnity, the insured can make a profit from an insurance claim. Reason (R): Indemnity means compensating only the actual loss.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: indemnity prevents profit. R is true.

qa.q: A policy under which the sum assured is paid only on the death of the insured is a
qa.a: whole life policy
qa.e: Whole life pays the beneficiaries after the insured's death.

qa.q: Under which policy is the amount paid in regular instalments after the insured reaches a certain age?
qa.a: Annuity policy
qa.e: Annuities provide regular income, often after retirement.

qa.q: A husband and wife take one policy on both their lives; the sum is paid to the survivor on the first death. This is a
qa.a: joint life policy
qa.e: Joint life policies cover two or more lives together.

qa.q: In life insurance, insurable interest must exist
qa.a: at the time of taking the policy
qa.e: For life insurance, interest is required when the policy is taken.

qa.q: Why is life insurance not a contract of indemnity?
qa.a: Because the loss of life cannot be measured in money
qa.e: Indemnity requires measurable financial loss.

qa.q: Why has health insurance become more important in India?
qa.a: Rising medical costs can create huge unexpected bills for families
qa.e: Health cover protects families from large medical expenses.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Life insurance is also called life assurance. Reason (R): Death is certain to happen; only its timing is uncertain, so the payment is assured.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; certainty of the event is why the term 'assurance' is used.

qa.q: Parents take a policy that pays a sum when their daughter turns 18, for her college fees. This is a
qa.a: children's endowment policy
qa.e: It is designed for children's education or marriage needs.

qa.q: Insurance of the ship itself against perils of the sea is called
qa.a: hull insurance
qa.e: Hull refers to the body of the vessel.

qa.q: In marine insurance, insurable interest must exist
qa.a: at the time of loss
qa.e: For marine insurance, it is required at the time of loss.

qa.q: In fire insurance, insurable interest must exist
qa.a: both at the time of contract and at the time of loss
qa.e: Fire insurance needs insurable interest at both times.

qa.q: Which of the following is NOT an element of fire insurance?
qa.a: The fire may be deliberately caused by the insured
qa.e: The fire must be accidental; deliberate fire is not covered.

qa.q: Which type of insurance policy has a surrender value?
qa.a: Life insurance
qa.e: Only life policies can be surrendered for a value before maturity.

qa.q: A fire policy is usually taken for a period of
qa.a: one year
qa.e: Fire policies are normally annual and renewable.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Fire insurance is a contract of indemnity. Reason (R): In fire insurance, the actual loss can be measured in money.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; because the loss is measurable, the insurer can compensate exactly that amount.

qa.q: Mehta & Co. ships 1,000 bales of cotton to Dubai and insures the bales against loss at sea. This is
qa.a: cargo insurance
qa.e: Insurance of goods carried on a ship is cargo insurance.

qa.q: Which postal service is meant for sending valuable articles with compensation for loss in transit?
qa.a: Insured post
qa.e: Insured post compensates up to the insured value.

qa.q: Money orders and the Public Provident Fund are examples of the post office's
qa.a: financial facilities
qa.e: They relate to saving and transferring money.

qa.q: A company advertises its new soap on postcards issued by India Post. This is
qa.a: media post
qa.e: Media post lets businesses advertise through postal stationery.

qa.q: Registered post is mainly used to
qa.a: ensure safe delivery with proof of posting and delivery
qa.e: Registration gives a record of posting and delivery.

qa.q: Paying electricity and phone bills at the post office is made possible through
qa.a: e-bill post
qa.e: E-bill post collects bill payments for service providers.

qa.q: Which of these is an allied (value-added) postal service?
qa.a: Speed post
qa.e: Speed post is an allied service; the others are financial facilities.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Post offices help in spreading financial services to rural areas. Reason (R): Post offices have a very wide network reaching remote villages and offer savings schemes.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; the wide network is why they can extend financial services to rural India.

qa.q: Direct post is used to
qa.a: deliver advertising material directly to targeted households
qa.e: Direct post is a form of direct advertising.

qa.q: E-business refers to
qa.a: conducting industry, trade and commerce using computer networks
qa.e: E-business covers all business activities done electronically.

qa.q: Which statement correctly relates e-business and e-commerce?
qa.a: E-commerce is a part of e-business
qa.e: E-business includes e-commerce plus internal functions.

qa.q: Which of these is part of e-business but NOT e-commerce?
qa.a: Managing employee records online
qa.e: Internal functions such as HR are e-business but not e-commerce.

qa.q: Digitisation of business means
qa.a: carrying out business activities through digital technologies such as computers and the internet
qa.e: Business processes shift to digital modes.

qa.q: E-commerce mainly covers a firm's interactions with
qa.a: customers and suppliers
qa.e: E-commerce is the buying and selling side of e-business.

qa.q: A firm uses an online platform to coordinate production between its plants in Pune and Chennai. This activity is
qa.a: e-business, but not e-commerce
qa.e: Coordinating internal production electronically is e-business.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-business has a wider scope than e-commerce. Reason (R): E-business includes internal functions like production, finance and HR along with buying and selling.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; including internal functions is why e-business is wider.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-commerce includes all internal activities of a business conducted online. Reason (R): E-commerce covers buying and selling over the internet.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: internal activities are e-business, not e-commerce. R is true.

qa.q: A company sells mobile phones directly to buyers through its website. This is
qa.a: B2C commerce
qa.e: A business selling to final consumers is B2C.

qa.q: An automobile company places orders for components with its suppliers through an online system. This is
qa.a: B2B commerce
qa.e: Both parties are businesses, so it is B2B.

qa.q: Selling second-hand books to other individuals through an online platform is
qa.a: C2C commerce
qa.e: Consumers sell to consumers using the platform.

qa.q: Linking the marketing, production and finance departments of a firm through an internal network is
qa.a: intra-B commerce
qa.e: Interaction within one firm is intra-B.

qa.q: A firm collects feedback from its online customers and offers after-sales support by chat. This falls under
qa.a: B2C commerce
qa.e: B2C includes not only sales but also customer support and feedback.

qa.q: Which benefit is typically associated with B2B e-commerce?
qa.a: Faster procurement and lower inventory because suppliers are linked electronically
qa.e: Electronic links with suppliers speed up ordering and reduce stock levels.

qa.q: Assertion (A): C2C commerce suits goods for which there are no well-established markets, such as used items. Reason (R): C2C platforms bring individual buyers and sellers together.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; by connecting individual buyers and sellers, platforms create a market for such goods.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A garment exporter buying fabric online from a textile mill is an example of B2C. Reason (R): In B2B commerce, both parties to the transaction are business firms.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: both parties are businesses, so it is B2B. R is true.

qa.q: On which basis does traditional business score better than e-business?
qa.a: Opportunity for inter-personal touch
qa.e: Face-to-face dealings give more personal touch.

qa.q: The cost of setting up an e-business is generally
qa.a: low, because physical premises and large inventories are not essential
qa.e: No need for shops, showrooms or heavy staffing at the start.

qa.q: Transaction risk is higher in e-business mainly because
qa.a: parties are far apart and may be anonymous
qa.e: Distance and anonymity make fraud and default more likely.

qa.q: Which is true of locational requirements?
qa.a: E-business has no locational requirement; traditional business needs proximity to raw materials or markets
qa.e: E-business can be run from anywhere with connectivity.

qa.q: Nature of contact with customers in e-business is
qa.a: direct
qa.e: Firms can deal directly with customers online.

qa.q: Response time to customer queries in e-business is
qa.a: instantaneous or very quick
qa.e: Electronic communication allows instant responses.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-business has greater ease of global reach than traditional business. Reason (R): The internet allows a firm's website to be accessed from anywhere in the world.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; global internet access is why the reach is greater.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Physical pre-sampling of products is easier in e-business. Reason (R): E-business does not require physical presence of the seller.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: pre-sampling is easier in traditional stores. R is true.

qa.q: E-business requires lower investment mainly because
qa.a: it does not need costly physical premises and large inventory to start
qa.e: Online businesses can begin with limited infrastructure.

qa.q: The ability to shop at 2 a.m. on a website illustrates which benefit of e-business?
qa.a: Convenience (24 × 7 access)
qa.e: The internet lets business run round the clock.

qa.q: An Indian handicraft seller gets orders from Germany and Japan through her website. This shows
qa.a: global reach
qa.e: Online presence opens worldwide markets.

qa.q: Booking an e-ticket instead of a printed ticket is an example of
qa.a: movement towards a paperless society
qa.e: Electronic documents replace paper.

qa.q: Downloading software immediately after paying online shows the benefit of
qa.a: speed
qa.e: Digital products can be delivered instantly.

qa.q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of e-business?
qa.a: High personal touch with every customer
qa.e: Low personal touch is actually a limitation of e-business.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-business offers convenience to customers. Reason (R): Customers can access an online business anytime and from anywhere.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; anytime-anywhere access is exactly what makes it convenient.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-business increases the use of paper in business. Reason (R): E-business uses electronic documents and records.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: e-business reduces paper use. R is true.

qa.q: Information and orders move at the speed of light, but goods take days to deliver. This limitation is called
qa.a: incongruence between order taking and delivery speed
qa.e: The mismatch between instant ordering and slower delivery is incongruence.

qa.q: Why is e-business less suitable for custom-tailored clothes?
qa.a: Because of low personal touch and no physical pre-sampling
qa.e: Such goods need fitting and personal interaction.

qa.q: A company secretly reads all employee emails. This raises which limitation of e-business?
qa.a: Ethical fallouts
qa.e: Monitoring employees online raises ethical and privacy concerns.

qa.q: Many senior citizens hesitate to shop online because they fear fraud. This is
qa.a: people's resistance
qa.e: Reluctance to adopt new technology is people's resistance.

qa.q: Risk in e-business increases due to anonymity because
qa.a: it is hard to verify the identity and location of the parties
qa.e: Without physical presence, cheats may hide their identity.

qa.q: Which is NOT a limitation of e-business?
qa.a: Global reach
qa.e: Global reach is a benefit.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-business suffers from low personal touch. Reason (R): Transactions take place through electronic networks without face-to-face interaction.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; no face-to-face meeting is exactly why personal touch is low.

qa.q: Assertion (A): In e-business, physical goods are delivered as fast as orders are placed. Reason (R): E-business transactions are conducted electronically.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: delivery is slower than ordering (incongruence). R is true.

qa.q: The 'shopping cart' is used in which stage of an online transaction?
qa.a: Ordering stage
qa.e: Items are collected in the cart before placing the order.

qa.q: Creating an account with name, address and password on a shopping site is part of the
qa.a: pre-purchase/sale stage (registration)
qa.e: Registration happens before ordering.

qa.q: A buyer pays in cash to the delivery agent when the parcel arrives. The payment mode is
qa.a: cash on delivery
qa.e: COD means paying cash on receipt of goods.

qa.q: Which goods can be delivered instantly over the internet?
qa.a: Software and e-books
qa.e: Digital products are delivered online.

qa.q: Under the cheque mode of online payment, the seller usually dispatches goods
qa.a: after the cheque is cleared
qa.e: Sellers wait for clearance to avoid the risk of dishonour.

qa.q: Digital cash is
qa.a: electronic money used to make online payments
qa.e: It exists only in electronic form.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Registration is generally the first step for buying from many online stores. Reason (R): The seller needs the buyer's contact and delivery details to process orders.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; the need for buyer details explains why registration comes first.

qa.q: Which is the correct order of stages in an online transaction?
qa.a: Pre-purchase/registration → ordering → delivery
qa.e: Registration comes first, then ordering, then delivery.

qa.q: A seller claims he never received an order that the buyer placed online. This is a
qa.a: transaction risk (default on order taking)
qa.e: Disputes about whether an order was placed or received are transaction risks.

qa.q: Converting data into a secret code that only authorised parties can read is called
qa.a: encryption
qa.e: Encryption protects data during storage and transmission.

qa.q: A virus corrupts a company's stored customer records. This risk relates to
qa.a: data storage and transmission
qa.e: Viruses threaten stored data.

qa.q: A buyer pays online but the goods never arrive. This is a
qa.a: default on delivery
qa.e: Failure to deliver after payment is a delivery default.

qa.q: Which of these is a resource required for successful e-business?
qa.a: Technically competent staff
qa.e: Skilled staff are needed to run and maintain online systems.

qa.q: Copying an online seller's original product photos and descriptions without permission threatens
qa.a: intellectual property
qa.e: Content and designs are intellectual property that can be misused online.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Encryption makes online transactions safer. Reason (R): Encrypted data cannot be read by unauthorised people even if it is intercepted.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; unreadable intercepted data is what makes the transaction safer.

qa.q: Assertion (A): E-business needs no payment or delivery systems. Reason (R): E-business is conducted over computer networks.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: efficient payment and delivery systems are essential resources. R is true.

qa.q: Social responsibility of business refers to
qa.a: the obligation to make decisions and take actions that are desirable in terms of society's objectives and values
qa.e: SR links business decisions with society's values.

qa.q: How does social responsibility differ from legal responsibility?
qa.a: SR is wider and largely voluntary, while legal responsibility is compulsory obedience to law
qa.e: Legal duties are a part of SR, but SR also includes voluntary actions.

qa.q: Which of the following is an example of legal responsibility?
qa.a: Paying income tax as required by law
qa.e: Paying taxes is required by law.

qa.q: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with Corporate Social Responsibility?
qa.a: Section 135
qa.e: Section 135 requires certain companies to spend on CSR.

qa.q: A company follows all labour laws and, in addition, offers free day-care for workers' children. The day-care shows
qa.a: social responsibility beyond legal requirements
qa.e: It is a voluntary benefit beyond the law.

qa.q: A socially responsible business considers the impact of its decisions on
qa.a: owners, workers, consumers, government, community and the environment
qa.e: SR looks at all stakeholders.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Social responsibility is broader than legal responsibility. Reason (R): Social responsibility includes legal obligations and also voluntary actions for society's welfare.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; including voluntary actions on top of legal duties is what makes SR broader.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Social responsibility is the same as legal responsibility. Reason (R): Legal responsibility is enforced by the state.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: SR is wider. R is true.

qa.q: 'Business exists to serve society, so its growth depends on serving society well.' This argument for SR is
qa.a: justification for existence and growth
qa.e: Business is justified only if it serves society's needs.

qa.q: A company voluntarily reduces emissions so that the government does not need to impose strict new rules. Which argument does this show?
qa.a: Avoidance of government regulation
qa.e: Voluntary responsibility reduces the need for regulation.

qa.q: Which argument says business has the finance and talented managers to solve social problems?
qa.a: Availability of resources with business
qa.e: Business has large resources that can be used for social good.

qa.q: A firm that caused land pollution helps clean up the area. This follows the argument of
qa.a: holding business responsible for social problems
qa.e: Business created part of the problem, so it should help solve it.

qa.q: 'A better society means a better place to do business.' This is the argument of
qa.a: better environment for doing business
qa.e: A healthy society improves business conditions.

qa.q: Social unrest and protests against a company can threaten its operations. Which argument for SR does this support?
qa.a: Maintenance of society
qa.e: Responsible behaviour helps maintain peace and order, avoiding public anger.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Social responsibility is in the long-term interest of the firm. Reason (R): Serving society builds a good public image, which helps the firm in the long run.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; the good image created explains the long-term benefit.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Business has no resources to deal with social problems. Reason (R): Converting problems into opportunities is an argument for social responsibility.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: business has considerable resources. R is true.

qa.q: 'The only responsibility of business is to earn maximum profits.' This argument against SR is
qa.a: violation of profit-maximisation objective
qa.e: Critics see SR as conflicting with the profit goal.

qa.q: Critics argue that the cost of social programmes will be recovered from buyers through higher prices. This is
qa.a: burden on consumers
qa.e: Costs passed on through prices burden consumers.

qa.q: 'Managers are not trained to solve social problems.' This argument is
qa.a: lack of social skills
qa.e: Business expertise does not equal social expertise.

qa.q: Which force has made business more socially responsible?
qa.a: Impact of consumer consciousness
qa.e: Aware consumers demand better behaviour from firms.

qa.q: Strong trade unions demanding fair treatment of workers show the force of
qa.a: pressure of labour movement
qa.e: Organised labour pushes firms towards responsibility.

qa.q: Professional managers, unlike owner-managers, tend to consider the interests of all stakeholders. This reflects
qa.a: development of a professional managerial class
qa.e: Professional management broadened business goals.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Lack of broad public support is an argument against social responsibility. Reason (R): The public generally does not like business to get involved in social programmes, so such programmes are hard to run successfully.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; because the public does not back business-run social programmes, they are hard to run, which is why this is used as an argument against SR.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Lack of social skills is an argument in favour of social responsibility. Reason (R): Business managers are mainly trained to handle business matters.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: it is an argument against SR. R is true.

qa.q: A company donates ₹50 lakh to build a library in a village. This is
qa.a: discretionary responsibility
qa.e: A purely voluntary contribution is discretionary.

qa.q: Producing goods that society wants and selling them at a profit is
qa.a: economic responsibility
qa.e: This is the basic economic role of business.

qa.q: Respecting the dignity of people in advertisements, even when the law does not require it, is
qa.a: ethical responsibility
qa.e: Expected but unwritten behaviour is ethical.

qa.q: Following the Factories Act and paying taxes honestly is
qa.a: legal responsibility
qa.e: Obeying laws is legal responsibility.

qa.q: Which kind of responsibility is purely voluntary?
qa.a: Discretionary
qa.e: Discretionary responsibilities are entirely at the firm's choice.

qa.q: Case: 'Sunrise Foods decides not to advertise its legal but sugary snack with cartoon characters aimed at small children.' Which responsibility is shown?
qa.a: Ethical responsibility
qa.e: The act is not required by law but expected by society.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Paying taxes is an example of legal responsibility. Reason (R): Payment of taxes is required by law.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; tax payment is a legal duty, which is why it falls under legal responsibility.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Donating to charity is a legal responsibility of every business. Reason (R): Discretionary responsibility includes voluntary acts like charity.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: charity is discretionary, not a legal duty for every business. R is true.

qa.q: Providing a fair and regular return on investment is a responsibility towards
qa.a: shareholders
qa.e: Owners expect a fair return on their capital.

qa.q: Respecting workers' right to form unions is a responsibility towards
qa.a: workers
qa.e: Workers have a right to organise.

qa.q: Avoiding adulteration and misleading advertisements is a responsibility towards
qa.a: consumers
qa.e: Consumers must get genuine products and honest information.

qa.q: Paying taxes honestly and respecting laws is a responsibility towards
qa.a: the government
qa.e: Good corporate citizenship includes honest tax payment.

qa.q: Which is a responsibility of business towards the community?
qa.a: Protecting the natural environment
qa.e: Business must not damage the community's environment.

qa.q: Giving shareholders regular, accurate and full information about the company is a responsibility towards
qa.a: shareholders
qa.e: Owners have a right to know how their company is doing.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A business should provide after-sales service to consumers. Reason (R): Consumers need support for repairs, maintenance and complaints after buying products.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; consumers' need for support is why after-sales service is a responsibility.

qa.q: Case: 'Bright Textiles installs fire exits, gives medical insurance to staff and consults worker representatives before changing shifts.' Its responsibility is mainly towards
qa.a: workers
qa.e: Safety, welfare and democratic consultation concern employees.

qa.q: Dumping of toxic industrial waste on open land causes
qa.a: land pollution
qa.e: Toxic waste damages the quality and fertility of land.

qa.q: Which is a reason for controlling pollution that directly benefits the firm's finances?
qa.a: Cost savings from efficient processes and reduced risk of liability
qa.e: Less waste means lower costs, and less pollution reduces damages claims.

qa.q: A firm may have to pay damages to people harmed by its pollution. Controlling pollution therefore results in
qa.a: reduced risk of liability
qa.e: Victims can claim compensation; less pollution, less liability.

qa.q: Which is a role of business in protecting the environment?
qa.a: Adopting clean technology and scientific waste disposal
qa.e: Clean technology and proper disposal reduce pollution.

qa.q: Noise from factories and vehicles can lead to
qa.a: stress and hearing problems
qa.e: Noise pollution harms health and well-being.

qa.q: Top management's definite commitment to environmental protection is important because
qa.a: it creates a culture of environmental care across the whole organisation
qa.e: Commitment at the top guides policies and employee behaviour.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Pollution control improves the public image of a business. Reason (R): People increasingly prefer firms that care about the environment.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; growing public concern is why environmental care improves image.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Business has no role in protecting the environment; it is only the government's job. Reason (R): Businesses can take part in government programmes such as cleaning rivers and planting trees.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: business has an important role. R is true.

qa.q: Business ethics refers to
qa.a: socially determined moral principles that should govern business activities
qa.e: Ethics are moral standards for business conduct.

qa.q: A whistle-blower system for employees to report unethical practices is an example of
qa.a: establishment of compliance mechanisms
qa.e: Compliance mechanisms ensure the code is actually followed.

qa.q: Why is top management commitment considered the most important element of business ethics?
qa.a: Because employees follow the example set by leaders
qa.e: Leaders set the tone; without their commitment, ethics will not take root.

qa.q: A written document covering honesty, product safety and fair marketing practices is the
qa.a: code of ethics
qa.e: Publishing a code is a key element of business ethics.

qa.q: Regular audits to check whether ethical standards are being followed reflect
qa.a: measuring results
qa.e: Results must be measured to see if ethics are working.

qa.q: Ethics programmes succeed only when employees at all levels
qa.a: are involved in implementing them
qa.e: Employees put ethics into practice, so involvement is vital.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Publication of a code alone is not enough to make a business ethical. Reason (R): Compliance mechanisms and top management commitment are also needed to put the code into practice.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; without commitment and compliance, a code remains on paper.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Business ethics and the law are exactly the same. Reason (R): Business ethics are socially determined moral principles.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: ethics go beyond law. R is true.

qa.q: Funds required to buy land, building and machinery are called
qa.a: fixed capital requirements
qa.e: Fixed capital is invested in long-lasting fixed assets.

qa.q: Which is an internal source of finance?
qa.a: Retained earnings
qa.e: Retained earnings are generated within the business.

qa.q: Long-term sources of finance are generally for a period of
qa.a: more than 5 years
qa.e: Long-term finance is for more than five years.

qa.q: Which of these is a short-term source of finance?
qa.a: Trade credit
qa.e: Trade credit is usually for a few weeks or months.

qa.q: Which is a feature of borrowed funds?
qa.a: They carry a fixed charge of interest and are repayable after a fixed period
qa.e: Borrowed funds have fixed interest and repayment obligations.

qa.q: Owners' funds differ from borrowed funds in that owners' funds
qa.a: are a permanent source with no fixed obligation to pay a return
qa.e: Owners' funds remain invested and returns depend on profits.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Collection of receivables is an internal source of finance. Reason (R): Funds released by collecting dues from debtors are generated within the business.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; such funds come from the firm's own operations, so they are internal.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Debentures are part of owners' funds. Reason (R): Debenture holders lend money to the company.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: debentures are borrowed funds. R is true.

qa.q: Equity shareholders are
qa.a: owners of the company
qa.e: Equity capital is ownership capital.

qa.q: The right of existing equity shareholders to be offered new shares first is the
qa.a: pre-emptive right
qa.e: New issues are first offered to existing holders as right shares.

qa.q: A company earns ₹6,00,000 distributable profit, pays preference dividend of ₹1,00,000 and has 50,000 equity shares. If the remainder is fully distributed, what is the dividend per equity share?
Why is the cost of equity capital generally higher than that of other sources?
qa.a: Dividends are not tax-deductible and issue costs are high
qa.e: Equity investors expect more for their risk, dividends come after tax, and issue costs are large.

qa.q: Which is a merit of equity shares for the company?
qa.a: There is no compulsion to pay dividend if profits are low
qa.e: Dividend is paid only if profits and the board allow.

qa.q: Equity shareholders have a residual claim, which means they are paid
qa.a: after preference shareholders and creditors have been paid
qa.e: They get what is left after others' claims.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Equity shares are a permanent source of capital. Reason (R): Equity capital is repaid only when the company is wound up.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; repayment only on winding up is why it is permanent.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Issue of fresh equity shares never affects the control of existing shareholders. Reason (R): Equity shareholders have voting rights.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: new equity can dilute control. R is true, and is the very reason dilution happens.

qa.q: Preference shareholders enjoy preference over equity shareholders regarding
qa.a: payment of dividend and repayment of capital
qa.e: These are the two preferential rights.

qa.q: Under which type of preference shares does unpaid dividend accumulate and get paid later?
qa.a: Cumulative preference shares
qa.e: Arrears are carried forward for cumulative shares.

qa.q: A company has ₹4,00,000 of 9% cumulative preference shares and paid no dividend last year. This year profits are sufficient. Total preference dividend payable this year is
qa.e: Annual dividend = ₹36,000; with one year's arrears, the total is ₹72,000.

qa.q: A company has ₹4,00,000 of 9% non-cumulative preference shares and paid no dividend last year. This year profits are sufficient. The preference dividend payable this year is
qa.e: Arrears lapse for non-cumulative shares; only the current year's ₹36,000 is paid.

qa.q: Preference shares that can be changed into equity shares after a period are
qa.a: convertible preference shares
qa.e: Convertible shares can be turned into equity.

qa.q: Which is a limitation of preference shares for the company?
qa.a: Dividend is not tax-deductible, making them costlier than debt
qa.e: Preference dividend is paid out of after-tax profits.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Preference shares do not dilute the control of equity shareholders. Reason (R): Preference shareholders generally do not have voting rights except on matters affecting their own rights.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; limited voting is why control is not diluted.

qa.q: On which basis do equity and preference shares differ?
qa.a: Equity dividend fluctuates with profits, while preference dividend is at a fixed rate
qa.e: Preference dividend is fixed; equity dividend varies.

qa.q: Retained earnings are a source of finance that is
qa.a: internal and part of owners' funds
qa.e: Profits kept back belong to owners and come from within.

qa.q: A company's profit is ₹80,00,000 and it distributes ₹30,00,000 as dividend. Retained earnings are
Why is it said that retained earnings have 'no explicit cost'?
qa.a: No interest, dividend or issue expenses have to be paid to raise them
qa.e: There is no direct cash cost, though there is an opportunity cost.

qa.q: Which is a limitation of retained earnings?
qa.a: Excessive ploughing back may dissatisfy shareholders who get lower dividends
qa.e: Shareholders may want higher dividends now.

qa.q: Retained earnings are an uncertain source because
qa.a: profits fluctuate from year to year
qa.e: If profits fall, less can be retained.

qa.q: Ignoring the opportunity cost of retained earnings may lead to
qa.a: sub-optimal use of the funds
qa.e: Managers may treat the funds as free and use them inefficiently.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Ploughing back of profits does not dilute control. Reason (R): No new shares are issued when profits are retained.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; since no new shares are issued, control stays unchanged.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Retained earnings are an external source of finance. Reason (R): Retained earnings are a permanent source of funds.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: they are internal. R is true.

qa.q: Debenture holders are
qa.a: creditors of the company
qa.e: Debentures are borrowed capital.

qa.q: A company issues ₹50,00,000 of 8% debentures. The annual interest is
Why is debt financing generally cheaper than equity for a company?
qa.a: Interest on debentures is a tax-deductible expense
qa.e: Tax deductibility reduces the effective cost of debt.

qa.q: Debentures that can be transferred merely by delivery are
qa.a: bearer debentures
qa.e: Bearer debentures pass by hand delivery.

qa.q: Interest of ₹3,00,000 is paid on debentures. If the tax rate is 25%, how much tax does the company save because of this interest?
Which is a limitation of debentures for the company?
qa.a: Fixed interest must be paid even when profits are low
qa.e: The fixed burden can strain the company in lean years.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Debenture holders are paid interest even if the company makes a loss. Reason (R): Interest on debentures is a charge against profit and a legal obligation.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; being a legal charge, interest must be paid irrespective of profit.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Debenture holders have the right to vote at general meetings of the company. Reason (R): Debentures are an acknowledgement of debt by the company.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: debenture holders are creditors without voting rights. R is true.

qa.q: Which is a merit of loans from commercial banks?
qa.a: Secrecy is maintained, since information is not disclosed to the public
qa.e: Bank dealings are private.

qa.q: Financial institutions such as IFCI and SFCs were set up mainly to provide
qa.a: long and medium-term finance to industry
qa.e: They fill the gap in long-term industrial finance.

qa.q: A firm borrows ₹8,00,000 at 12% simple interest per year for 2 years. Total interest payable is
Which is a limitation of loans from financial institutions?
qa.a: They may nominate directors on the company's board, restricting management
qa.e: Nominee directors can limit the freedom of management.

qa.q: Bank loans are considered a flexible source because
qa.a: the loan amount can be increased or repaid early as the business needs
qa.e: Borrowings can be adjusted to needs.

qa.q: Which is a limitation of bank loans?
qa.a: Renewal or extension of the loan is uncertain
qa.e: Short-term loans may not be renewed when needed.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Financial institutions provide funds even during periods of depression. Reason (R): Financial institutions are development-oriented bodies set up by governments to support industry.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; their development role is why they lend even when other sources dry up.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Borrowing from a bank requires the issue of a prospectus to the public. Reason (R): Bank loans are a source of borrowed funds.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: no prospectus is needed for a bank loan. R is true.

qa.q: Trade credit is
qa.a: credit extended by one trader to another when goods are bought on credit
qa.e: It is supplier's credit for goods bought.

qa.q: In the books of the buyer, trade credit appears as
qa.a: sundry creditors or accounts payable
qa.e: The buyer owes money to suppliers, so they are creditors.

qa.q: A supplier offers 3% cash discount on goods worth ₹2,00,000 if paid at once. A buyer instead uses 90 days' credit. What discount does he lose?
Which is a limitation of trade credit?
qa.a: It may induce a firm to indulge in overtrading
qa.e: Easy credit can tempt firms to buy beyond their ability.

qa.q: Inter-corporate deposits are
qa.a: unsecured short-term deposits made by one company with another
qa.e: ICDs are company-to-company short-term deposits.

qa.q: An inter-corporate deposit that can be withdrawn by the lender on one day's notice is a
qa.a: call deposit
qa.e: Call deposits are repayable on call.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Trade credit is readily available to a buyer with a good reputation. Reason (R): Suppliers are willing to sell on credit to buyers whose creditworthiness is known.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; known creditworthiness is why credit is readily given.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The ICD market is a well-organised, regulated market. Reason (R): Inter-corporate deposits are made by one company with another.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the ICD market is unorganised. R is true.

qa.q: A company sells its receivables to a specialised agency that collects them and pays the company in advance. This is
qa.a: factoring
qa.e: The agency is called a factor.

qa.q: Commercial paper is
qa.a: an unsecured promissory note issued to raise short-term funds
qa.e: CP is short-term and unsecured.

qa.q: In lease financing, the owner of the asset who gives it on rent is the
qa.a: lessor
qa.e: The lessor owns; the lessee uses.

qa.q: Which is a merit of lease financing for the lessee?
qa.a: The asset can be used without a large initial investment
qa.e: Leasing saves the upfront cost.

qa.q: Which is a limitation of commercial paper?
qa.a: Only financially sound, highly rated firms can issue it
qa.e: Weak firms cannot access CP.

qa.q: Which is a merit of public deposits for the company?
qa.a: Simple procedure and no charge on assets
qa.e: Raising deposits involves fewer formalities and needs no mortgage.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Commercial paper is a continuous source of funds. Reason (R): A maturing commercial paper can be repaid by issuing a fresh commercial paper.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; rolling over CPs is what makes the source continuous.

qa.q: Assertion (A): In leasing, the lessee bears the risk of the asset becoming obsolete. Reason (R): In leasing, the lessor retains ownership of the asset.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the lessor bears obsolescence risk. R is true.

qa.q: A firm needs funds to buy machinery that will last 15 years. Based on purpose and time period, it should use
qa.a: a long-term source such as debentures or equity
qa.e: Long-lived assets need long-term funds.

qa.q: Which factor favours debt over equity because interest is deductible from taxable profits?
qa.a: Tax benefits
qa.e: Tax deductibility of interest lowers the effective cost of debt.

qa.q: A firm with highly fluctuating profits should avoid heavy reliance on
qa.a: debt with fixed interest
qa.e: Fixed interest is a burden when profits fall.

qa.q: A partnership firm cannot raise funds by issuing shares. This is the factor of
qa.a: form of organisation and legal status
qa.e: Legal form decides which sources are available.

qa.q: From the company's point of view, which source carries the least risk?
qa.a: Equity shares
qa.e: Equity has no fixed charge or repayment obligation.

qa.q: Which factor considers both issue expenses and the cost of using the funds?
qa.a: Cost
qa.e: Cost includes procurement and utilisation costs.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A company wanting to retain control may prefer debentures to equity shares. Reason (R): Debenture holders do not have voting rights.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; no voting rights for debenture holders is why control is retained.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Short-term needs should be met through long-term sources like equity. Reason (R): Purpose and time period are factors in choosing sources of funds.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: short-term needs should be met by short-term sources. R is true.

qa.q: The MSMED Act, 2006 classifies enterprises into
qa.a: manufacturing and service enterprises
qa.e: It separates enterprises producing goods from those providing services.

qa.q: Under the revised (composite) criteria, an enterprise is classified as micro, small or medium on the basis of
qa.a: investment in plant and machinery or equipment, and annual turnover
qa.e: Both investment and turnover limits must be satisfied.

qa.q: Udyam Registration of MSMEs is
qa.a: an online, free registration based on self-declaration
qa.e: It is a paperless, Aadhaar-based process on the Udyam portal.

qa.q: An enterprise's turnover exceeds the limit for a micro enterprise though its investment is within the micro limit. It will be classified as
qa.a: a small enterprise (if within small limits)
qa.e: Exceeding either limit moves the unit to the next category.

qa.q: Under the revised criteria, the limits for manufacturing and service enterprises are
qa.a: the same
qa.e: A common set of limits now applies to both.

qa.q: Which is a benefit of Udyam registration for a small unit?
qa.a: Easier access to government schemes and priority-sector credit
qa.e: Registration helps units access support schemes and loans.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The government revises MSME limits from time to time. Reason (R): Inflation and economic growth make old investment and turnover limits outdated.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; changing economic conditions are why limits are revised.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The MSMED Act, 2006 deals only with manufacturing enterprises. Reason (R): The MSMED Act, 2006 provides for the development of micro, small and medium enterprises.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: it covers both manufacturing and service enterprises. R is true.

qa.q: Using the limits in force from 1 April 2025, a unit has investment of ₹2 crore in plant and machinery and an annual turnover of ₹40 crore. It is classified as a
qa.a: small enterprise
qa.e: Investment (₹2 crore) is within the micro limit of ₹2.5 crore, but turnover (₹40 crore) crosses the micro limit of ₹10 crore. Both figures are within the small limits (₹25 crore and ₹100 crore), so it is a small enterprise.

qa.q: Small industries are the largest source of employment in India after
qa.a: agriculture
qa.e: They are second only to agriculture in providing jobs.

qa.q: Setting up small units in backward rural areas helps in
qa.a: balanced regional development
qa.e: Spreading industry across regions reduces regional imbalance.

qa.q: How do village industries help reduce rural-to-urban migration?
qa.a: By providing non-farm employment and income within villages
qa.e: Local jobs reduce the need to move to cities.

qa.q: Which is NOT a role of small business in India?
qa.a: Creating monopoly power in national markets
qa.e: Small businesses usually face competition; they do not create national monopolies.

qa.q: Small businesses can take quick decisions mainly because
qa.a: the owner is usually the manager and need not consult many people
qa.e: Fewer layers mean faster decisions.

qa.q: Handloom weavers working from home in a village is an example of
qa.a: cottage industry
qa.e: Cottage industries are run by families using local skills.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Small businesses help in using local resources. Reason (R): Small units are often located near the source of raw materials and local skilled labour.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; being located close to local inputs is why they use local resources.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Small industries increase the migration of rural people to cities. Reason (R): Small industries provide employment in rural areas.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: they reduce migration. R is true.

qa.q: A small unit cannot get a bank loan because it has no assets to offer as security. This is the problem of
qa.a: finance
qa.e: Lack of collateral restricts access to credit.

qa.q: Small businesses often pay more for raw materials because
qa.a: they buy in small quantities and have low bargaining power
qa.e: Small purchases do not attract bulk discounts.

qa.q: Under-use of installed machines due to lack of demand is the problem of
qa.a: capacity utilisation
qa.e: Idle capacity raises costs per unit.

qa.q: Which is an external cause of sickness in small units?
qa.a: Delayed payments by buyers
qa.e: Delayed payments come from outside the unit.

qa.q: After liberalisation, small units in India face tougher
qa.a: global competition from large and multinational firms
qa.e: Opening the economy brought competition from bigger firms.

qa.q: A small unit relies on middlemen who pay low prices for its products. This is a
qa.a: marketing problem
qa.e: Weak marketing makes units depend on middlemen.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Small units often suffer from low productivity. Reason (R): Many small units use outdated technology.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; outdated technology is a key reason for low productivity.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Small businesses face no problem of finance because banks prefer them. Reason (R): Small businesses often lack collateral and credit history.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: finance is a major problem. R is true and is one reason for it.

qa.q: NSIC was set up in
qa.e: The National Small Industries Corporation was established in 1955.

qa.q: District Industries Centres were launched on
qa.e: DICs began on 1 May 1978.

qa.q: Supplying machines to small units on easy hire-purchase terms is a function of
qa.a: NSIC
qa.e: NSIC provides machinery on hire purchase.

qa.q: Which agency acts as a single window for small industries at the district level?
qa.a: District Industries Centre
qa.e: DICs bring all support under one roof locally.

qa.q: Which is NOT a function of NSIC?
qa.a: Registering partnership firms
qa.e: Partnership registration is done by the Registrar of Firms.

qa.q: DICs mainly promote
qa.a: small, tiny, village and cottage industries
qa.e: Their focus is grassroots small industries.

qa.q: Assertion (A): DICs make it easier for rural entrepreneurs to start units. Reason (R): DICs provide a range of services such as project identification, finance and raw material support at one place in the district.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; the single-window district-level support is why starting becomes easier.

qa.q: Assertion (A): NSIC works only for large industries. Reason (R): NSIC was set up to promote and support small industries.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: NSIC serves small industries. R is true.

qa.q: The person who sets up a business enterprise is called the
qa.a: entrepreneur
qa.e: The entrepreneur creates the enterprise.

qa.q: The business organisation created through the process of entrepreneurship is the
qa.a: enterprise
qa.e: Enterprise is the outcome of entrepreneurship.

qa.q: 'Entrepreneurship requires skills that can be learnt.' This describes entrepreneurship as a
qa.a: systematic activity
qa.e: Skills and knowledge can be developed through learning and practice.

qa.q: An entrepreneur introduces a new method of packaging that keeps food fresh longer. This characteristic is
qa.a: innovation
qa.e: New products or processes are innovation.

qa.q: Bringing together land, labour, capital and technology to produce goods describes
qa.a: organisation of production
qa.e: The entrepreneur coordinates the factors of production.

qa.q: Entrepreneurs generally take
qa.a: moderate, calculated risks
qa.e: They weigh risks and rewards carefully.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Entrepreneurship is described as a lawful and purposeful activity. Reason (R): Its aim is to create value within the framework of law.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; operating within law to create value is what lawful and purposeful means.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Entrepreneurship and employment are the same. Reason (R): Entrepreneurship involves setting up one's own business.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: employment means working for others. R is true.

qa.q: Entrepreneurship helps capital formation because
qa.a: it mobilises savings of people into productive investment
qa.e: Entrepreneurs channel savings into businesses.

qa.q: Which is the first step in starting a new venture?
qa.a: Identifying a business opportunity
qa.e: Everything begins with spotting an opportunity.

qa.q: A document describing the product, market, competitors, operations and financial projections of a proposed venture is the
qa.a: business plan
qa.e: A business plan guides the venture and attracts funding.

qa.q: Checking whether there is enough demand and whether the idea is technically and financially viable is the step of
qa.a: evaluating the idea through feasibility study
qa.e: Evaluation tests the idea before investing.

qa.q: How does entrepreneurship improve economic efficiency?
qa.a: Through innovation that produces more output from the same inputs
qa.e: New methods and products raise productivity.

qa.q: Which is NOT a contribution of entrepreneurship to economic development?
qa.a: Increasing unemployment
qa.e: Entrepreneurship reduces unemployment.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Entrepreneurship is needed for the economic development of a country. Reason (R): Entrepreneurs increase production, create jobs and mobilise savings for investment.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; these contributions are why entrepreneurship drives development.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A business plan is prepared after the enterprise has grown and expanded. Reason (R): A business plan helps an entrepreneur obtain funds.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the plan comes before resources are mobilised and the venture is launched. R is true.

qa.q: Startup India was launched on
qa.a: 16 January 2016
qa.e: The initiative began on 16 January 2016.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three action-plan areas of Startup India?
qa.a: Nationalisation of start-ups
qa.e: Startup India supports private start-ups; it does not nationalise them.

qa.q: A founder uses her own savings and early sales revenue to run her start-up. This is
qa.a: bootstrapping
qa.e: Self-funding is bootstrapping.

qa.q: Raising small contributions from a large number of people through an online platform is
qa.a: crowdfunding
qa.e: The 'crowd' provides funds.

qa.q: Professionally managed funds that invest in high-growth start-ups in exchange for equity are called
qa.a: venture capital
qa.e: Venture capital funds are managed by professionals.

qa.q: How does a business accelerator differ from an incubator?
qa.a: An accelerator runs a short, intensive programme to speed up growth of existing start-ups, while an incubator nurtures early ideas over a longer period
qa.e: Incubators nurture; accelerators speed up.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Angel investors usually invest at an early stage of a start-up. Reason (R): Angel investors are individuals with surplus funds who back promising new ventures in exchange for equity.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; their role of backing new ventures is why they come in early.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Microfinance institutions give very large loans to big corporations. Reason (R): Microfinance provides small loans to people who lack access to regular banking.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: microfinance means small loans for small borrowers. R is true.

qa.q: Which IPR protects a newly invented machine that is new, inventive and industrially useful?
qa.a: Patent
qa.e: Patents protect inventions.

qa.q: Computer software is protected in India mainly under
qa.a: copyright
qa.e: Software is treated like a literary work under copyright law.

qa.q: In India, a patent is granted for a term of
qa.a: 20 years
qa.e: A patent lasts 20 years.

qa.q: 'Kanchipuram silk' can be sold under that name only if it comes from the specified region. This is protected by
qa.a: geographical indication
qa.e: GI links product quality to its place of origin.

qa.q: A firm registers a unique bottle shape for its perfume. The IPR involved is
qa.a: design
qa.e: Designs protect the visual shape or pattern of an article.

qa.q: Why should a start-up protect its intellectual property?
qa.a: To prevent copying, build brand value and attract investors
qa.e: IPR protects innovation and increases the value of the venture.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A registered trademark helps customers identify a firm's products. Reason (R): A trademark distinguishes the goods or services of one firm from those of others.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; distinguishing goods is exactly how it helps identification.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A geographical indication protects a new invention. Reason (R): A geographical indication identifies goods as originating from a particular place.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: inventions are protected by patents. R is true.

qa.q: Internal trade refers to
qa.a: buying and selling of goods and services within the boundaries of a nation
qa.e: It takes place within the country.

qa.q: Why is no customs duty levied on internal trade?
qa.a: Because goods are produced and sold within the same country
qa.e: Customs duty applies to goods crossing national borders.

qa.q: By buying goods in bulk from manufacturers, wholesalers help them in
qa.a: facilitating large-scale production
qa.e: Bulk orders allow manufacturers to produce on a large scale.

qa.q: A wholesaler pays a manufacturer in cash on delivery of goods. This is the service of
qa.a: financial assistance
qa.e: Cash payment frees manufacturers' funds.

qa.q: Wholesalers allow retailers to buy goods and pay later. This service is
qa.a: grant of credit
qa.e: Credit lets retailers keep shops stocked without immediate cash.

qa.q: Wholesalers bear risks such as fall in prices, theft and spoilage of goods in stock. This service is mainly for
qa.a: manufacturers
qa.e: By taking delivery and holding stock, they relieve manufacturers of these risks.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Wholesalers help retailers to operate with less stock. Reason (R): Retailers can buy small quantities from wholesalers whenever needed.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; frequent small purchases are why retailers need less stock, reducing their risk.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Wholesalers mainly sell goods to final consumers. Reason (R): Wholesalers buy goods in large quantities from manufacturers.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: they sell to retailers and businesses. R is true.

qa.q: A retailer sells goods mainly to
qa.a: final consumers for personal use
qa.e: Retailers are the last link in distribution.

qa.q: By telling customers about newly launched products, a retailer provides
qa.a: new products information
qa.e: Retailers inform consumers about new arrivals.

qa.q: Retailers help manufacturers by passing on feedback about consumers' tastes. This service is
qa.a: collecting market information
qa.e: Retailers are in direct contact with consumers.

qa.q: A retailer keeps many brands and sizes of shampoo so that customers can choose. This is
qa.a: wide selection
qa.e: Variety lets consumers compare and choose.

qa.q: Home delivery and installation of an air conditioner by the shop are examples of
qa.a: after-sales services
qa.e: Services after the sale are after-sales services.

qa.q: Because retailers handle sales to millions of consumers, manufacturers and wholesalers are freed to focus on
qa.a: large-scale operations
qa.e: Retailers enable large-scale operations of producers.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Retailers help in the promotion of products. Reason (R): Retailers arrange displays and in-store promotions that attract customers.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; displays and promotions are how retailers promote products.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Retailers sell goods in large quantities to other businesses. Reason (R): Retailers are the last link between producers and consumers.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: they sell in small quantities to final consumers. R is true.

qa.q: Retailers who do not have a fixed place of business are called
qa.a: itinerant retailers
qa.e: Itinerant means moving from place to place.

qa.q: A vendor sells vegetables from a handcart in residential lanes every morning. He is a
qa.a: peddler/hawker
qa.e: He carries goods door to door.

qa.q: A trader sells clothes at a weekly market in one town on Mondays and another on Fridays. He is a
qa.a: market trader
qa.e: Market traders open at different places on fixed days.

qa.q: Pavement vendors selling newspapers and snacks near railway stations are
qa.a: street traders
qa.e: They locate where floating population is large.

qa.q: What distinguishes cheap jacks from hawkers?
qa.a: Cheap jacks have temporary shops in a locality and change locality; hawkers move door to door
qa.e: Cheap jacks have a temporary base; hawkers keep moving.

qa.q: Itinerant retailers generally deal in
qa.a: low-value consumer goods of daily use
qa.e: They sell common items like vegetables, snacks and toys.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Itinerant retailers provide convenience to consumers. Reason (R): They take goods to the customer's doorstep or to busy places where people already are.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; reaching customers where they are is what gives convenience.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Street traders choose quiet, remote places to sell their goods. Reason (R): Street traders sell common-use items.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: they choose places with huge floating population. R is true.

qa.q: A shop in a residential colony selling groceries, toiletries and stationery for daily needs is a
qa.a: general store
qa.e: General stores meet day-to-day needs of nearby residents.

qa.q: A shop that sells only men's formal shirts is a
qa.a: speciality shop
qa.e: It specialises in one specific type within the clothing line.

qa.q: A store dealing in all varieties of computers and laptops of many brands is a
qa.a: single line store
qa.e: It sells one product line in wide variety.

qa.q: Shops selling used furniture and old books at low prices are
qa.a: second-hand goods shops
qa.e: They deal in used goods.

qa.q: Small vendors with fixed stalls at street crossings selling hosiery and toys are
qa.a: street stall holders
qa.e: They have a small fixed stall at busy spots.

qa.q: Compared with itinerant retailers, fixed-shop retailers usually
qa.a: have greater resources and offer services like home delivery and credit
qa.e: Permanent premises and resources allow more services.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Fixed-shop retailers enjoy more customer trust than itinerant retailers. Reason (R): Fixed-shop retailers have a permanent place, so customers can return for complaints and services.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both are true; a permanent address is why customers trust them more.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A speciality shop sells a wide variety of unrelated products for daily needs. Reason (R): General stores stock a variety of products for daily needs.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: that describes a general store; a speciality shop sells a specific type of product. R is true.

qa.q: A large store with separate departments for clothing, electronics, furniture and groceries under one roof is a
qa.a: departmental store
qa.e: Many departments under one roof is the departmental store.

qa.q: Departmental stores are usually located
qa.a: in central locations of cities
qa.e: A central location attracts customers from all over the city.

qa.q: Which is a merit of departmental stores?
